info.title: Frappé API
info.description: The HTTP API of Frappé. Every endpoint lives under `/v1`; errors are RFC 9457 Problem Details.

get.description: The session the request authenticated with: when it idles out, when it ends whatever its use, and until when its step-up still counts (null when none was made or it has run out). Every authenticated request moves the idle expiry on, never past the absolute one. The session is the bearer token or the console cookie of the request; 401 identity.session.invalid when there is none, or it is unknown, expired, revoked, opened under credentials that changed, or the cookie is sent twice.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: The languages the client accepts (BCP 47, with q weights). Frappé is written in en, es, es-AR, es-MX, pt-BR; the ranges are tried from the highest quality down and the first one served wins (fr, es-AR;q=0.8 answers in es-AR). Another Spanish answers in es, any Portuguese in pt-BR, and anything else, or no header, in English. Content-Language names the language served.

Content-Language.description: The languages Frappé's own texts in the response are written in; absent when it holds none, only proper nouns, identifiers and source data (names and categories as their source publishes them).

Cache-Control.description: no-store: no cache may keep the answer, and it carries no validator.

delete.description: Ends the session the request authenticated with: its token stops working at once, and the console cookie is cleared. A request that carries the cookie must come from a console origin (403 http.origin.forbidden otherwise); one that carries a bearer token is not checked. 401 identity.session.invalid when the request has no valid session.

post.description: Registers an owner with a name, an email address and a password, and mails a six-digit code to the address. The language of the mail is the one the request negotiates from Accept-Language (an unknown one is answered in English, never refused). It answers 201 with an id to verify the address with. The answer is the same for an address that is new, one a pending owner holds (the new registration takes it over, and the old code stops working) and one a verified owner holds (nothing is written and that owner is told by mail), so it never reveals whether an address is registered. The same Idempotency-Key registers once. 400 identity.email.invalid or identity.name.invalid (a name is at most 60 characters, given plus family, and holds no http, www. or ://), 422 for a password that is too short, too long or breached.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes the request safe to retry: the first successful (2xx) answer is stored for 24 hours and replayed, with Idempotent-Replayed: true, to every later request with the same key, caller and content, without running it again. Send a new key (a UUID is fine) for each new request. 400 platform.idempotency_key.invalid for a key that is not 1 to 255 printable characters without spaces or is sent twice; 422 platform.idempotency_key.reused when the key was used for a different request; 409 platform.idempotency_key.in_progress while the first request still runs; 503 platform.idempotency.unavailable when answers cannot be kept (the request was not run). A refused or failed request is not stored, so it can be retried with the same key. Cookies are never replayed.

Cache-Control.description: no-store: no cache may keep the answer, and it carries no validator.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: true when this is the stored answer of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key; absent on the first answer.

post.description: Proves the address with the code that was mailed: the owner becomes active and a session opens, so the owner needs no log-in. The session is in the body (send its token as Authorization: Bearer) and, for the web console, in the session cookie. 422 identity.code.invalid for a code that is wrong, expired, used or replaced and for an id that is unknown or malformed (one answer for all of them); a code takes five guesses. 503 identity.attempts.unavailable when guesses cannot be counted.

post.description: Mails a new verification code to a pending owner, which replaces the one before it. It answers 202 always, for an id that is unknown, malformed, verified or over its budget of five codes an hour, so it reveals nothing about which owners exist.

post.description: Resend reports delivered, bounced, complained, delayed and suppressed messages here. The body is Resend's event as JSON. The call must carry Resend's Svix signature headers: svix-id (the event's unique id), svix-timestamp (the signing time, in Unix seconds) and svix-signature (one or more space-separated v1,<base64> HMAC-SHA256 signatures of '{svix-id}.{svix-timestamp}.{body}' under the webhook secret), with a timestamp within 5 minutes of now; otherwise it is answered 400 notifications.webhook_signature.invalid. Every authentic call is answered 204, whether or not the module tracks the event, and a repeated event changes nothing. 409 means a concurrent duplicate of the same event was being written: Resend redelivers it and the retry is answered 204. 503 means the database is unavailable, and Resend retries too. A body over 64 KiB is answered 413.

post.description: The one-click unsubscribe of RFC 8058, for the link of a marketing email. The query token is the signed credential of the link (signed, not hidden: it is not encrypted): it names the recipient and the category (only marketing can be turned off) and never expires. It answers 204 when the category is off for the recipient, including when it already was, and 400 notifications.unsubscribe_token.invalid for a token that is missing, tampered, not issued here or not written exactly as issued (padded, re-encoded). The body may be the form of RFC 8058 (List-Unsubscribe=One-Click), urlencoded or multipart, or none; it is not read, and any other type is answered 415. It never redirects.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The opaque signed token of the unsubscribe link in the email. A missing one is answered 400.

examples.title: The resource does not exist.
examples.detail: The URL does not match any endpoint of the API.

errors.message: The URL does not match any endpoint of the API.

type.description: The category of the failure: urn:frappe:problem: and a stable slug. It never names an error code. The list of categories grows: a client handles a category it does not know by its HTTP status.

title.description: Stable summary of the category, in the language of Content-Language.

detail.description: The error's text when there is one, or how many errors there are, in the language of Content-Language.

errors.description: Every error found, so a client can fix them all at once.

traceId.description: W3C trace id of the request, to find it in the logs and traces.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details. type is the category of the failure; the error codes are only in errors, which always lists every error, one or several.

parameters.description: The values the error was raised with, by name (the same the texts use).

message.description: The error in the language of Content-Language; absent when no text exists.

ProblemError.description: One error: its stable code, the values it was raised with and its text in the response language.

List-Unsubscribe.description: Always One-Click (RFC 8058). The route ignores the value.
